newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AGASSI SET TO BREAK OUT OF SLUMP FOR DAVIS CUP CAUSE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI SET TO BREAK OUT OF SLUMP FOR DAVIS CUP CAUSE.

text.p: Andre Agassi is hoping his fervor for Davis Cup competition will be just the thing to help him break out of his current slump and U.S. captain Tom Gullikson is counting on it.

Agassi is a miserable 3-5 in tournament play this year with four opening-match defeats. But the former number one takes an impressive 22-4 singles record and a 13-match Davis Cup winning streak into this weekend's quarter-final tie against the Netherlands.
"My game is right there waiting to come alive and certainly the intensity of Davis Cup will add a certain element that brings out the best," Agassi said following Thursday's draw ceremony.
"It's helpful to him that he's playing for a greater cause than just himself," said Gullikson. "He's used to playing big matches. It tends to bring out the best in him."
Agassi, whose ranking is down to 29th in the world, opens the tie Friday against 68th-ranked Dutch Davis Cup newcomer Sjeng Schalken.

Jim Courier, another former number one who has been moving back up the rankings lately, plays Jan Siemerink in Friday's second singles. In Saturday's doubles, Gullikson sends Rick Leach and Jonathan Stark against Paul Haarhuis and Jacco Eltingh.

Both sides will be without their biggest guns on the hard courts of the Palisades Tennis Club with top-ranked Pete Sampras and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek both declining to play for their countries at this stage.

But Gullikson said he was pleased with the draw that sends Agassi out first, with Courier, who won both his singles in Brazil in the first round, set to play the inexperienced Schalken in a potential fifth and deciding match Sunday.
"I like that matchup for us," Gullikson said. "Andre's record speaks for itself in Davis Cup, and Schalken to my knowledge hasn't played a singles match in Davis Cup."
Netherlands captain Stan Franker, whose squad beat Romania in the opening round, expects the 20-year-old Schalken will rise to the occasion.
"Sjeng is our youngest and inexperienced in Davis Cup but I think he is ready to do something big this weekend," Franker said.
Haarhuis also thinks his young teammate could well surprise the home side.
"He is just going out there and hit those balls on the lines," Haarhuis predicted. "The crowds will be quiet, they will be awed and I think this young boy can do it."
Still Franker is taking little comfort from Agassi's recent travails.
"He is struggling on Tour, but that doesn't necessarily mean he is going to struggle in a Davis Cup tie," Franker said of Agassi.
"Davis Cup is totally different from the tour. Andre has proven by winning the Olympics for instance, that even in a bad year, he can come out and pull off a win like that."
Agassi is looking for just such a reversal of fortune when he comes out swinging Friday.
"Friday is going to be one of those days that you go out there and make it happen," the former Wimbledon and U.S. Open champion said.
"You have just got to go out there and do it. That's why we're here," Agassi said.
"I am more than ready to be here and excited about playing. There is no better time than right here in Davis Cup."
